Hi @eng-93! Yes, for STOCKFLOW-104 (weighted_average_cost), the design review agreed that rounding should be half-up (e.g., 100.5 -> 101) to match the finance stock ledger. You should avoid round-half-to-even and keep the arithmetic in integers.

Hi! Regarding your question about average_daily_demand: The handover notes I have state that demand is net of customer returns - RTN records are subtracted from shipped total before averaging. If returns exceed shipments, demand is 0 (never negative). So RTN does subtract from net demand, which matches what you described. The edge case is just ensuring we don't go negative.

Hi @eng-88! I checked my notes. For reorder_point, it was agreed in the design review that planning uses a rolling four-week window: only the most recent 28 entries of daily_demand are used, both for the cycle demand and for the safety_stock call. Shorter histories are used as they are.

Hi @eng-56, regarding the design review for allocate_freight: it was agreed that when fractional remainders tie, the leftover cent goes to the line with the larger value first. Only when values are equal does the earlier line win.

Hi @eng-91! Yes, the design review decision for `stock_valuation` was that only positive stock is valued. SKUs whose (combined) on-hand is zero or negative are left out of the rows and the total entirely (negative stock must not reduce the reported value), and they do not need cost layers.
